description: Na₅Fe₂P₂(CO₇)₂ crystallizes in the monoclinic Pm space group. There are three inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.36-2.77 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.34-2.70 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.26-2.52 Å. There are two inequivalent Fe sites. In the first Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 2.07-2.34 Å. In the second Fe site, Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form distorted FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.98-2.12 Å. There are two inequivalent C sites. In the first C site, C is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to three O atoms. There is one shorter (1.29 Å) and two longer (1.30 Å) C-O bond lengths. In the second C site, C is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to three O atoms. There are a spread of C-O bond distances ranging from 1.26-1.33 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 40-46°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.53-1.59 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four FeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 45-59°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.54-1.58 Å. There are twelve inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na and one C atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to three Na, one Fe, and one C atom. In the third O site, O is bonded to three Na, one Fe, and one C atom to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₃FeC trigonal bipyramids. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one P atom to form distorted ONa₂FeP tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one ONa₃FeC trigonal bipyramid and corners with two equivalent ONa₂FeC trigonal pyramids. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one C atom to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₂FeC trigonal pyramids. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to two equivalent Na, one Fe, and one C atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to four Na and one C atom. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the twelfth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one Fe, and one P atom.
